meta.title: Directive 2010/64/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 20 October 2010 on the right to interpretation and translation in criminal proceedings

items.heading: Article 1

items.text: 1. This Directive lays down rules concerning the right to interpretation and translation in criminal proceedings and proceedings for the execution of a European arrest warrant.
items.comment: No specific legal instrument was enacted in Portugal with a view to implementing this Directive, as existing legislation, notably the Code of Criminal Procedure, was deemed to accommodate in full the norms established in this Directive. In our view, the majority of the norms of the Directive are in effect sufficiently covered by previous legislation, although this might not be true for all of them, as expounded subsequently.

items.text: 2. The right referred to in paragraph 1 shall apply to persons from the time that they are made aware by the competent authorities of a Member State, by official notification or otherwise, that they are suspected or accused of having committed a criminal offence until the conclusion of the proceedings, which is understood to mean the final determination of the question whether they have committed the offence, including, where applicable, sentencing and the resolution of any appeal.

nationalActs.titleEn: Code of Criminal Procedure (Decree-Law no. 78/87, of 17 February)

provisions.comment:
Articles 254 to 261 CCP, mentioned above, regulate the conditions in which a person may be arrested. Arrest (or detention) is different from pre-trial custodial detention, as outlined shortly below. It should be noted that, under Portuguese law, arrest and pre-trial custodial detention may not to be regarded as investigative measures, as they are not aimed at collecting evidence. Arrest is conceived of as a “cautionary measure” (medida cautelar) and custodial detention as a “coercive measure” (medida de coacção), and they serve different purposes:

a) Arrest is regulated mainly in Articles 254 f., according to which a person can be arrested in order to be tried within a maximum term of 48 hours under a special (more expeditious) form of proceedings called “summary proceedings” (processo sumário), or to have a coercive measure applied to him/her. It is also possible to arrest a person in order to take him/her immediately – or, if this is not possible, within a maximum term of 24 hours – to a judicial authority for attending a procedural act. When a person has been arrested in order to be tried under summary proceedings but this turned out not to be possible, or to be subjected to a coercive measure, this person must be interrogated by a judge within a maximum term of 48 hours (first judicial interrogation). Arrest in flagrante delicto is possible only for offences punishable with imprisonment (which applies, a fortiori, to the arrest of a person who has not been caught in flagrante delicto). Arrest without flagrante delicto may only take place based on an order of a judge or, if pre-trial custodial detention is admissible in the case, by the Public Prosecution, provided that there is good reason to believe that the person would not present him/herself spontaneously before a judicial authority within the due term. In case of urgency, even if there is no flagrante delicto, the police may arrest a person, but this arrest must be communicated either to a judge or to the Public Prosecution (depending on its purpose) for validation. The defendant may appeal these decisions, and habeas corpus against unlawful detention may be invoked by any citizen in the exercise of his/her political rights. It is also possible to arrest a person if his/her extradition has been requested and a judge finds the request to be prima facie viable. Finally, a person may also be arrested if a EAW has been duly issued, although this type of arrest must still comply with the provisions of the CCP on arrest, outlined above. 

b) Pre-trial custodial detention can only be applied if there is “strong evidence” (fortes indícios) that the defendant has intentionally committed an offence punishable with imprisonment for over 5 years, or for over 3 years in some cases. This measure can also be applied, regardless of a specific degree of suspicion and of the offence in question, if the person is requested for extradition. As for the EAW, the CCP does not explicitly establish that receiving one such request enables the authorities to apply this measure, but the Supreme Court has ruled that the EAW, as a swifter form of extradition, abides by the same rules as classic extradition insofar as this issue is concerned. As all other coercive measures regulated in the CCP, pre-trial custodial detention may only be applied if: (i) the defendant has escaped or there is a risk that he/she will escape; (ii) there is a risk that he/she will disturb the investigation, notably the gathering of evidence or its veracity, by destroying or tampering with it; or (iii) there is a risk that the defendant will continue his/her criminal activity or cause severe public upheaval. On the other hand, custodial detention – as well as house arrest (obrigação de permanência na habitação) – can only be applied where other coercive measures which do not involve deprivation of liberty show inadequate or ineffective. This measure can only be ordered by a judge, after hearing the defendant in the mandatory presence of his/her lawyer, except for cases of justified impossibility, and it may not be based upon facts or elements which are not provided or communicated to the defendant during that hearing. 

This measure is subject to maximum terms which are established in the CPP (Article 215), and that the decision to apply this measure (or to maintain it, if it had already been applied) can be appealed against, an appeal which must be ruled on within a maximum term of 30 days. Again, any citizen in the exercise of his/her political rights may file a habeas corpus request against illegal imprisonment as a means to react against the application of pre-trial custodial detention.
provisions.textEn:
(1) Without detriment to Article 57, the designation as defendant (arguido) is also mandatory as soon as:

(a) A person makes statements before any judicial authority or criminal police body during an inquiry initiated against him/her, where there are grounds to suspect that such person has committed a criminal offence;

(b) A coercive or patrimonial guarantee measure must be imposed on him/her;

(c) A suspect is arrested under the terms and for the purposes of Articles 254 to 261 of this Code; or

(d) A police report has been drawn up identifying a person as an alleged offender and that person has been informed on the contents thereof, unless the report is clearly unfounded.

(2) The status of defendant is acquired with the communication to the concerned person, either orally or in writing, by a judicial authority or criminal police body that, as of that moment, he/she has the status of defendant in criminal proceedings and, if necessary, by the explanation of procedural rights and duties of defendants laid down in Article 61, which he/she is thenceforth bound to observe.

(3) If the act is carried out by the criminal police, it must be communicated to a judicial authority within 10 days, so that this authority may, within another 10-day term, examine and decide whether or not the act is to be considered valid.

(4) The status of arguido implies the delivery to the concerned person, if possible simultaneously, of a document specifying details on the case and on the defence attorney, if one has already been appointed, and such a document must also indicate the rights and duties that the person is thenceforth entitled to.

(5) Failure to comply with the formalities laid down in this Article carry a prohibition to use as evidence any statements made by the concerned person.

(6) The non-validation of the act designating a person as arguido by the judicial authority does not affect the evidence that has been previously collected.

(1) If a founded suspicion emerges during the course of an interrogation of a person who is not a defendant has committed an offence, the authority performing such an interrogation shall suspend it immediately and effect the communication and the advice mentioned in Article 58 (2) CCP.

(2) A person suspected of having committed an offence has the right to be designated as a defendant at his/her own request, whenever an investigation is being carried out with a view to establishing his/her criminal liability and measures are being taken which personally affect him/her.

(3) The provisions of Article 58 (3) and (4) apply accordingly.

As of the moment when a person is assigned the status of defendant (arguido), he/she is entitled to exercise procedural rights and duties, without detriment to the application of coercive measures and measures of patrimonial guarantee, as well as the carrying out of evidentiary measures in the legally prescribed terms.

provisions.comment: This provision applies not only to defendants, but also to any other person intervening in a criminal procedure.
provisions.textEn:
(1) Portuguese is the language that must be used in all procedural acts, written as well as oral, or otherwise the act will be null.

(2) If a person must intervene in the criminal procedure who does not know or is not fluent in Portuguese, he/she is appointed a suitable interpreter, free of charge, even if the authority presiding over the act or any of the subjects of the procedure happen to know the language at issue.

(3) Defendants can choose, free of charge, to be assisted by an interpreter other than the one who was appointed to them, for the purposes of translating conversations held with their attorneys.

(4) Interpreters are obliged to secrecy [both ‘secrecy of justice’, which protects the contents of the procedure (when applicable), and to ‘professional secrecy’] and may not reveal the conversations held between the defendant and his/her attorney, whatever the phase is in which the procedure is at, or otherwise the interpreter will be breaching professional secrecy.

(5) Failure to comply with the provisions of paragraphs 3 and 4 carries that any evidence thereby obtained [notably, the statements made by the defendant] is null and cannot be used.

(6) An interpreter is also appointed when it is necessary to translate a document which is written in a foreign language and has not been subject to authenticated translation.

(7) Interpreters are appointed by a judicial authority [a public prosecutor or a judge] or by a criminal police authority.

items.text: 3. Where the law of a Member State provides for the imposition of a sanction regarding minor offences by an authority other than a court having jurisdiction in criminal matters, and the imposition of such a sanction may be appealed to such a court, this Directive shall apply only to the proceedings before that court following such an appeal.

4. This Directive does not affect national law concerning the presence of legal counsel during any stage of the criminal proceedings, nor does it affect national law concerning the right of access of a suspected or accused person to documents in criminal proceedings.
items.comment: The provisions of this Directive do not in any way affect the right of the defendant to have his/her attorney present at any stage of the criminal procedure nor does the right of the defendant to access documents in criminal proceedings.

items.heading: Article 2

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspected or accused persons who do not speak or understand the language of the criminal proceedings concerned are provided, without delay, with interpretation during criminal proceedings before investigative and judicial authorities, including during police questioning, all court hearings and any necessary interim hearings.

items.text: 3. The right to interpretation under paragraphs 1 and 2 includes appropriate assistance for persons with hearing or speech impediments.

nationalActs.titleEn: Code of Criminal Procedure (Decree-Law no. 78/87, of 17 February)

provisions.textEn:
(1) When a person who has a hearing or speech impediment [“um surdo, um deficiente auditivo ou um mudo”] is to make statements in the procedure, the following rules shall be complied with:

(a) In case of a hearing impediment, the person is appointed a suitable interpreter of sign language, lip-reading or written expression, depending on which is more adequate to the situation of the concerned person;

(b) In case of a speech impediment, if he/she can write, he/she is questioned orally and replies in writing; otherwise, if he/she so requests, a suitable interpreter is appointed.

(2) Absence of an interpreter carries the act to be postponed.

(3) The provisions of the previous paragraphs apply at every stage of the procedure and regardless of the status therewith held by the person in question.

(4) Article 92 (3) to (5) apply accordingly.

items.text: 4. Member States shall ensure that a procedure or mechanism is in place to ascertain whether suspected or accused persons speak and understand the language of the criminal proceedings and whether they need the assistance of an interpreter.

provisions.comment: Arguably, this would enable the defendant to request that an interpreter be appointed to him/her, if the authorities did not do so at their own initiative.
provisions.textEn: Unless otherwise provided for in the law, the defendant is specifically entitled, at all stages of the procedure, to the following rights: (…) to intervene in the investigation phases of the procedure, including by providing evidence or requesting that investigative measures be conducted.

Even if he/she is not deprived of liberty, the defendant may submit at any stage of the procedure written explanations (explicações), memoranda (memoriais), and requests (requerimentos), even if not signed by his/her attorney, as long as these documents relate to the object of the process or aim at safeguarding fundamental rights of the defendant. These documents are always inserted into the file concerning the criminal procedure at issue.

items.comment: No such specific procedure or mechanism is in place in the Portuguese legal system, at least it is not formally provided for in the law. The following provisions allow for the conclusion that Article 2 (4) and (5) of the Directive have been implemented into the Portuguese legal system, but only partially. Arguably, they are insufficient to meet the mechanisms envisioned in the Directive for controlling the need for, and the quality of the interpretation or translation.

items.text: 5. Member States shall ensure that, in accordance with procedures in national law, suspected or accused persons have the right to challenge a decision finding that there is no need for interpretation and, when interpretation has been provided, the possibility to complain that the quality of the interpretation is not sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.

provisions.comment:
Arguably, this enables the defendant to request that an interpreter be appointed to him/her, if the authorities did not do so at their own initiative. See also Article 98 (1) of the CCP (above, and again further below).

If the authority then refuses to appoint the interpreter, the defendant may invoke the nullity mentioned in Article 120 (2) (c) (below), and such decisions are open to appeal under the general principle set out in Article 399 of the CPP (further below).
provisions.textEn: Unless otherwise provided for in the law, the defendant is specifically entitled, at all stages of the procedure, to the following rights: (…) to intervene in the investigation phases of the procedure, including by providing evidence or requesting that investigative measures be conducted.

In addition to other circumstances provided for in the law, the following, if invoked by the interested procedural subject, will carry nullity: (...) The failure to appoint an interpreter in a case where the law commands such an appointment;

provisions.comment: None of the exceptions provided for in Article 400 of the CCP seems to apply here, since the decision not to appoint an interpreter cannot be construed as a mere administrative decision (Article 400 (1) (a)), nor as a decision that falls within the discretion of the court (Article 400 (1) (b)).
provisions.textEn: Any judicial decision may be appealed unless otherwise provided for in the law.

provisions.comment: This provision refers to expert witnesses, but it applies to interpreters, ex vi Article 92 (8) CCP. As for complains by the defendant on the quality of the interpretation provided, it is possible to proceed along the same lines mentioned above, on the basis of Articles 61 (1) (g), 120 (2) (c) and 399 CCP.
provisions.textEn: The judicial authority which appointed the [interpreter] may order his/her replacement when he/she (...) is performing in a careless manner the duties that have been assigned to him/her; this decision may not be appealed.

provisions.comment: By prohibiting certain individuals from participating in procedural acts because of meaningful doubts as to their impartiality, this provision increases the reliability of the interpretation services. This, however, still does not allow to conclude that this provision of the Directive is fully implemented in the Portuguese legal system.
provisions.textEn: The provisions of this Chapter of the CPP [on impediments, refusals and excuses (impedimentos, recusas e escusas) to participate in procedural acts] apply with due adaptations to expert witnesses, interpreters and justice officers.

provisions.comment: Again, this provision increases the reliability of the provided interpretation services, but it still does not allow for the conclusion that this provision of the Directive is fully implemented in the Portuguese legal system.

items.comment: As stated, no specific procedure or mechanism is in place to ascertain whether suspected or accused persons speak and understand the language of the criminal proceedings and whether they need the assistance of an interpreter. Consequently, no specific right is in place to challenge a decision finding that there is no need for interpretation, or, when interpretation has been provided, to complain about its quality. However, the following rules allow for the conclusion that this provision of the Directive has been partially implemented into the Portuguese legal system.

items.text: 6. Where appropriate, communication technology such as videoconferencing, telephone or the Internet may be used, unless the physical presence of the interpreter is required in order to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment:
No such possibilities are explicitly provided for in the Portuguese legal system. Rather, the rule is that these functions are carried out in person: see notably Articles 96, 158 (1) (b), 317 (1), 318, 328- A, 332– 334, 343, 350 (3), 355– 357, and 360– 361 of the CCP.

It is conceivable that an analogy may be established between interpreters and experts or other subjects who are allowed to intervene through video-link pursuant to Articles 158 (2), 317 (1) and 350 (3) CPP, but this is by no means certain, especially where the physical presence of the defendant in the procedural act in question is mandatory: in this case, it would seem that the physical presence of the interpreter is an inevitable consequence of the requirement that the defendant be physically present.

items.text: 7. In proceedings for the execution of a European arrest warrant, the executing Member State shall ensure that its competent authorities provide persons subject to such proceedings who do not speak or understand the language of the proceedings with interpretation in accordance with this Article.

nationalActs.title: Regime Jurídico do Mandado de Detenção Europeu (Lei n.º 65/2003, de 23 de Agosto)
nationalActs.titleEn: Law on the European Arrest Warrant (Law no. 65/2003, of 23 August)

provisions.textEn: The European Arrest Warrant shall be translated into one of the official languages of the executing Member State or another official language of the Institutions of the European Communities accepted by this State, by declaration deposited with the General Secretariat of the Council.
If the arrested person does not adequately understand or speak Portuguese, a suitable interpreter shall be provided free of charge.

Articles 57 to 67 of the CCP [on the formal designation of a person as a defendant (arguido), the rights and duties springing from this status, etc.] apply as appropriate, and the person sought on account of a EAW, when arrested, should be provided with a document informing him/her of the rights mentioned in the previous paragraphs.

provisions.comment: In consequence of this provision, as well as of Article 17 (4) of the LEAW, immediately above, all other provisions assigning the right to an interpreter to defendants in actual criminal proceedings (notably, Article 92 of the CCP, further above) apply also to persons sought pursuant to an EAW.
provisions.textEn: The Code of Criminal Procedure applies in a subsidiary manner to EAW proceedings.

items.text: 8. Interpretation provided under this Article shall be of a quality sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings, in particular by ensuring that suspected or accused persons have knowledge of the case against them and are able to exercise their right of defence.

nationalActs.title: Código de Processo Penal (Decreto-Lei n.º 78/87, de 17 de Fevereiro)
nationalActs.titleEn: Code of Criminal Procedure (Decree-Law no. 78/87, of 17 February)

provisions.comment: The fact that assistance by a lawyer is mandatory in each and every procedural act in the case of defendants unfamiliar with the Portuguese language contributes to the quality of the interpretation / translation, in that it is justified to assume that the lawyer will contribute to ensuring that proper interpretation / translation is being provided to his/her client.
provisions.textEn: [a]ssistance by an attorney is mandatory: (...) in any procedural act, save for the formal designation of the person as a defendant, whenever the person is [among other] unfamiliar with the Portuguese language.

items.comment: Article 2 (8) of the Directive is also to be regarded as already implemented. The concept of “quality sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings” is of a normative nature and has no explicit or direct equivalent in Portuguese law, but all the provisions indicated above which confer on defendants or persons sought pursuant to an EAW the right to an interpreter (notably Articles 92 CCP and 17 (3) LEAW) explicitly require the appointed interpreter to be “suitable”, which in this context should be read as ‘properly qualified’. Moreover, as also mentioned, there are other provisions aimed at securing the quality (notably Article 153 (3) CCP) and the impartiality (notably Articles 47 (1) and 91 CCP) of the interpretation / translation. Furthermore, Article 64 (1) (d) CCP prescribes that “[a]ssistance by an attorney is mandatory: (...) in any procedural act, save for the formal designation of the person as a defendant, whenever the person is [inter alia] unfamiliar with the Portuguese language”. The fact that assistance by a lawyer is mandatory in each and every procedural act in the case of defendants unfamiliar with the Portuguese language contributes to the quality of the interpretation / translation, in that it is justified to assume that the lawyer will contribute to ensuring that proper interpretation / translation is being provided to his/her client. Therefore, and in sum, while it may be debated whether Article 2 (4) and (5) are covered by Portuguese law – in that there is no specific procedure or mechanism aimed at ascertaining whether the person is in need of assistance by an interpreter, nor, accordingly, a specific remedy for challenging such a decision or for complaining about the quality of the interpretation –, it seems that the more general provision of Article 2 (8) is fully implemented, as several norms are in force which do seek to ensure a high level of reliability of interpretation services.

items.heading: Article 3
items.subHeading: Right to translation of essential documents

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspected or accused persons who do not understand the language of the criminal proceedings concerned are, within a reasonable period of time, provided with a written translation of all documents which are essential to ensure that they are able to exercise their right of defence and to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.

nationalActs.title: Código de Processo Penal (Decreto-Lei n.º 78/87, de 17 de Fevereiro)
nationalActs.titleEn: Code of Criminal Procedure (Decree-Law no. 78/87, of 17 February)

provisions.comment: Unlike the Directive, Portuguese law establishes no differentiation between essential and unessential documents, and thus Article 92 (6) applies to all documents. The dichotomy has in any case some equivalence in the dichotomy between documents the translation of which is “necessary” or “unnecessary”. If a document is deemed necessary by the defendant but its translation has not been officially ordered, the defendant may request that this be done, and if the request is denied he/she may appeal such a decision under the general right to appeal enshrined in Article 399 CCP. In the context of the EAW, the law does not explicitly require the warrant to be translated into a language that the sought person understands, but this solution is commanded by Article 92 (6) CCP.
provisions.textEn: An interpreter is also appointed when it is necessary to translate a document which is written in a foreign language and has not been subject to authenticated translation.

items.text: 2. Essential documents shall include any decision depriving a person of his liberty, any charge or indictment, and any judgment.

nationalActs.titleEn: Code of Criminal Procedure (Decree-Law no. 78/87, of 17 February)

provisions.textEn: An interpreter is also appointed when it is necessary to translate a document which is written in a foreign language and has not been subject to authenticated translation.

nationalActs.title: Regulamento Geral dos Estabelecimentos Prisionais (Decreto-Lei n.º 51/2011, de 11 de Abril)
nationalActs.titleEn: General Regulation of Prison Facilities (Decree-Law no. 51/2011, of 11 April)

provisions.textEn:
(1) Inmates are informed of their rights and duties, which, if necessary, are explained to them and translated.

(2) Inmates are provided with a booklet indicating their rights and duties, the norms in force which are relevant to the enforcement of the penalty or security measures to which they have been convicted, and the information necessary to their good integration in the prison facility, namely the services and activities which are available to them and the respective opening and closing hours, as well as the place where they may find the legislation and regulations relevant for the execution of said penalty or security measure.

(3) Prison facilities provide the booklet mentioned in the previous paragraph to the inmates in Portuguese language as well as in the languages spoken by most inmates.

nationalActs.title: Código da Execução das Penas e Medias Privativas da Liberdade  (Lei n.º 115/2009, de 12 de Outubro)
nationalActs.titleEn: Code of Enforcement of Penalties and Measures involving Deprivation of Liberty (Law no. 115/2009, of 12 October)

provisions.textEn: The enforcement of penalties and measures involving deprivation of liberty applied to inmates who are foreigners or belong to ethnic or linguistic minorities should, as much as possible, enable them to express their cultural values, to mitigate difficulties they might face in terms of social integration or command of the Portuguese language, namely by providing contact with consular or diplomatic authorities or organisations aimed at supporting immigrants, courses of Portuguese language, translation of documents or intervention of interpreters.
Inmates are immediately informed of their rights and duties, duly explained and if necessary translated (...).

nationalActs.titleEn: Regulation of the Detention Conditions in the Premises of the Judiciary Police and in Courts and Public Prosecution Services  (Dispatch no. 12786/2009, of 29 May)

items.text: 3. The competent authorities shall, in any given case, decide whether any other document is essential. Suspected or accused persons or their legal counsel may submit a reasoned request to that effect.

provisions.textEn: Unless otherwise provided for in the law, the defendant is specifically entitled, at all stages of the procedure, to the following rights: (…) to intervene in the investigation phases of the procedure, e.g. by providing evidence or requesting that investigative measures be conducted.

Even if he/she is not deprived of liberty, the defendant may submit at any stage of the procedure written explanations (explicações), memoranda (memoriais), and requests (requerimentos), even if not signed by his/her attorney, as long as these documents relate to the object of the process or aim at safeguarding fundamental rights of the defendant. These documents are always inserted into the file concerning the criminal procedure at issue.

items.text: 4. There shall be no requirement to translate passages of essential documents which are not relevant for the purposes of enabling suspected or accused persons to have knowledge of the case against them.
items.comment:
Please the provisions and comments of paragraphs (1) to (3) of this Article of the Directive.

Since the Portuguese system offers broader possibilities of translation than the Directive, by making no differentiation between essential and unessential documents, defendants may request even the translation of unessential documents pursuant to the provisions mentioned above, although arguably such a request may be refused by the authorities based on Article 92 (6) (see above) due to the translation being 'unnecessary'.

items.text: 5. Member States shall ensure that, in accordance with procedures in national law, suspected or accused persons have the right to challenge a decision finding that there is no need for the translation of documents or passages thereof and, when a translation has been provided, the possibility to complain that the quality of the translation is not sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.

nationalActs.titleEn: Code of Criminal Procedure (Decree-Law no. 78/87, of 17 February)

provisions.textEn: Unless the law provides otherwise, the defendant has, at all stages of the criminal procedure, the right: (…) To intervene in the inquiry and in the instruction, by presenting evidence and submitting requests to the authorities;

Even if he/she is not deprived of liberty, the defendant may submit at any stage of the procedure written explanations (explicações), memoranda (memoriais), and requests (requerimentos), even if not signed by his/her attorney, as long as these documents relate to the object of the process or aim at safeguarding fundamental rights of the defendant. These documents are always inserted into the file concerning the criminal procedure at issue.

items.text: 6. In proceedings for the execution of a European arrest warrant, the executing Member State shall ensure that its competent authorities provide any person subject to such proceedings who does not understand the language in which the European arrest warrant is drawn up, or into which it has been translated by the issuing Member State, with a written translation of that document.

nationalActs.title: Regime Jurídico do Mandado de Detenção Europeu (Lei n.º 65/2003, de 23 de Agosto)
nationalActs.titleEn: Law on the European Arrest Warrant (Law no. 65/2003, of 23 August)

provisions.textEn: Articles 57 to 67 of the CCP [on the formal designation of a person as a defendant (arguido), the rights and duties springing from this status, etc.] apply as appropriate, and the person sought on account of a EAW, when arrested, should be provided with a document informing him/her of the rights mentioned in the previous paragraphs.

provisions.comment: In consequence of this provision, as well as of Article 17 (4) of the LEAW, immediately above, all other provisions assigning the right to translation to defendants in actual criminal proceedings (notably, Article 92 of the CCP, further above) apply also to persons sought pursuant to an EAW.
provisions.textEn: The Code of Criminal Procedure applies in a subsidiary manner to EAW proceedings.

nationalActs.title: Código de Processo Penal (Decreto-Lei n.º 78/87, de 17 de Fevereiro)
nationalActs.titleEn: Code of Criminal Procedure (Decree-Law no. 78/87, of 17 February)

provisions.textEn: An interpreter is also appointed when it is necessary to translate a document which is written in a foreign language and has not been subject to authenticated translation.

items.comment: While LEAW does not explicitly requires the warrant to be translated into a language that the sought person understands, this solution is commanded by Article 92 (6) of the CCP, which applies to EAW proceedings ex vi Articles 17 (4) and 34 of the LEAW.

items.text: 7. As an exception to the general rules established in paragraphs 1, 2, 3 and 6, an oral translation or oral summary of essential documents may be provided instead of a written translation on condition that such oral translation or oral summary does not prejudice the fairness of the proceedings.
items.comment: No (optional) exception of that sort is provided for in Portuguese law. Some procedural acts are to be recorded in an abridged manner (see Article 100 (2) CCP), in which case a defendant who wishes to obtain a translation of the act’s official record will only be able to receive a translation of this abridged record. However, the most important procedural acts must be recorded in full.

items.text: 8. Any waiver of the right to translation of documents referred to in this Article shall be subject to the requirements that suspected or accused persons have received prior legal advice or have otherwise obtained full knowledge of the consequences of such a waiver, and that the waiver was unequivocal and given voluntarily.
items.comment: Portuguese law does not provide for the possibility to waive the right to an interpreter or to a translation in the cases where they are mandatory, meaning that this provision of the Directive lacks object.

items.text: 9. Translation provided under this Article shall be of a quality sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings, in particular by ensuring that suspected or accused persons have knowledge of the case against them and are able to exercise their right of defence.
items.comment: In similar terms as those expounded on Article 2 (8) of the Directive, Portuguese law does not make use of a normative criterion whereby the quality of the translation must be “sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings”. However, all the provisions indicated above which confer on defendants or persons sought pursuant to an EAW the right to an interpreter (notably Articles 92 CCP and 17 (3) LEAW) explicitly require the appointed interpreter to be “suitable”. The explanations provided above in this respect apply here, mutatis mutandis.

items.text: Member States shall meet the costs of interpretation and translation resulting from the application of Articles 2 and 3, irrespective of the outcome of the proceedings.
items.heading: Article 4

nationalActs.titleEn: Code of Criminal Procedure (Decree-Law no. 78/87, of 17 February)

provisions.textEn:
(...)

(2) If a person must intervene in the criminal procedure who does not know or is not fluent in Portuguese, he/she is appointed a suitable interpreter, free of charge, even if the authority presiding over the act or any of the subjects of the procedure happen to know the language at issue.

(3) Defendants can choose, free of charge, to be assisted by an interpreter other than the one who was appointed to them, for the purposes of translating conversations held with their attorneys.

(...)

items.heading: Article 5
items.subHeading: Quality of the interpretation and translation
items.comment:
Only partially implemented.

Articles 5 and 6 of the Directive, concerning the quality of interpretation and translation, require some considerations: the register(s) of independent translators / interpreters prescribed in paragraph (2) of Article 5, and, as far as was possible to establish, the training prescribed in Article 6, have not been implemented. This casts legitimate doubts as to the quality of interpretation and translation being provided in Portugal at present. Moreover, interpretation and translation in judicial proceedings may be considered as not well-paid, which certainly does not contribute to increasing quality, and no differentiation is even made depending on the language at issue.

items.text: 1. Member States shall take concrete measures to ensure that the interpretation and translation provided meets the quality required under Article 2(8) and Article 3(9).

nationalActs.title: Regulamento das Custas Processuais (Decreto-Lei n.º 34/2008, de 26 de Fevereiro)
nationalActs.titleEn: Regulation of Justice Fees (Decree-Law no. 34/2008, of 26 February)

provisions.comment: In turn, Table IV provides that translators shall be paid 1/3777 justice fee units per translated word, and interpreters shall be paid between 1 and 2 justice fee units per service. Each justice fee unit currently amounts to circa € 100.
provisions.textEn: The remuneration of [inter alia] translators and interpreters is made in accordance with the current provision and Table IV attached to the present Regulation.

items.comment: See the previous comment, as well as the comments and provisions inserted in Article 2 (5) and (8) and in Article 3 (5) e (9) of the Directive.

items.text: 2. In order to promote the adequacy of interpretation and translation and efficient access thereto, Member States shall endeavour to establish a register or registers of independent translators and interpreters who are appropriately qualified. Once established, such register or registers shall, where appropriate, be made available to legal counsel and relevant authorities.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.text: 3. Member States shall ensure that interpreters and translators be required to observe confidentiality regarding interpretation and translation provided under this Directive.

nationalActs.title: Código de Processo Penal (Decreto-Lei n.º 78/87, de 17 de Fevereiro)
nationalActs.titleEn: Code of Criminal Procedure (Decree-Law no. 78/87, of 17 February)

provisions.comment: The norms providing for the offences of breach of secrecy of justice and of professional secrecy are found in the Penal Code, Articles 195 f., 371 and 383 f.
provisions.textEn: Interpreters are obliged to secrecy [both to ‘secrecy of justice’, which protects the contents of the procedure (when applicable), and to ‘professional secrecy’] and may not reveal the conversations held between the defendant and his/her attorney, whatever the phase is in which the procedure is at, or otherwise the interpreter will be breaching professional secrecy.
Failure to comply with the provisions of paragraphs 3 and 4 carries that any evidence thereby obtained [notably, the statements made by the defendant] is null and cannot be used.

items.text: Without prejudice to judicial independence and differences in the organisation of the judiciary across the Union, Member States shall request those responsible for the training of judges, prosecutors and judicial staff involved in criminal proceedings to pay special attention to the particularities of communicating with the assistance of an interpreter so as to ensure efficient and effective communication.
items.heading: Article 6

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: As far as was possible to establish, no training is currently provided which comes even close to that envisaged by this provision of the Directive. See again the comment to Article 5 of the Directive, supra.

items.text: Member States shall ensure that when a suspected or accused person has been subject to questioning or hearings by an investigative or judicial authority with the assistance of an interpreter pursuant to Article 2, when an oral translation or oral summary of essential documents has been provided in the presence of such an authority pursuant to Article 3(7), or when a person has waived the right to translation pursuant to Article 3(8), it will be noted that these events have occurred, using the recording procedure in accordance with the law of the Member State concerned.
items.heading: Article 7

nationalActs.title: Código de Processo Penal (Decreto-Lei n.º 78/87, de 17 de Fevereiro)
nationalActs.titleEn: Code of Criminal Procedure (Decree-Law no. 78/87, of 17 February)

provisions.comment: Article 169 CCP provides that the facts reported in an authentic or authenticated document are considered proven insofar as the veracity of the document or of the information contained therein is not justifiably brought into question.
provisions.textEn:
(1) The procedural acts that the law requires to be recorded, as well as statements, requests, promotions and decisions orally uttered, must be recorded in a written document called ‘auto’ [hereinafter ‘official record’].

(...)

(3) An official record contains, in addition to those required for written acts, the following elements:

(a) The identification of the persons who took part in the procedural act;

(...)

(c) A detailed description of the operations carried out, of the intervention of each procedural participant, of the statements made, and of the manner and circumstances in which they were made, including the indication of the beginning and end of each statement, when an audio or audiovisual recording is to be made, of the documents that have been presented or received and of the results obtained, so as to guarantee a genuine record of the procedural act;

(d) Any occurrence which shows relevant for assessing the evidence or the lawfulness of the procedural act.

(4) Article 169 applies accordingly.

The interrogation of an arrested defendant is, as a rule, carried out under audio or audiovisual recording. Other means of recording, including stenographical or stenotypical or other means capable of ensuring a full reproduction or recording of the act, may be used only where the former means are unavailable, which must be recorded in the official act.
The procedural acts that are to be practised in writing must be drafted in a perfectly intelligible manner (...).
